name: J04 — large history, both clients, one product
about: The large-history dimension, in its own file so a blocked dimension
cannot block it.
THE SCENARIO ASSERTS MOVEMENT, not keystrokes. An earlier revision sent
PageUp three times and captured, which passed while the native client
could not scroll at all: its offset was capped by a count of slices while
a slice renders one row per line, so a 300-line answer moved the view by a
single row. A runner that presses a key and does not check the screen
moved is not a witness.
THE SAME KEY IS NOT THE SAME DISTANCE, and assuming it was is the defect
this revision fixes. The frozen keybindings do bind PageUp to a page-up
ACTION on both clients, and an earlier revision of this file concluded
from that the same keystroke was the same user action and gave both
clients twelve presses. The magnitudes are not the same:
native    app.rs:358          scrolls by the FULL viewport height
retained  index.tsx:382       scrolls by `scroll.height / 2`, a HALF page
An attended run showed exactly that. Twelve presses took the native client
to the top of the answer and left the retained client at lines 110-142,
and the shared assertion then reported a retained failure that was really
a scenario that had not pressed far enough. Equal key counts cannot
establish a shared reachability claim between clients that move by
different amounts.
So each client is now taken to the SAME ENDPOINTS and asserted there
SEPARATELY, and the differing cost is recorded rather than hidden: the
native assertion is made after twelve presses, the retained one after
thirty. Thirty is a bounded over-estimate, not a measurement — paging
clamps at the top, so surplus presses cost nothing and the count is chosen
to clear the distance with margin rather than to state a minimum.
THAT COST DIFFERENCE IS A REAL PRODUCT DIFFERENCE and is reported as one:
reaching the top of the same answer takes the retained client about twice
the presses. This scenario does not call that a regression. It is the
half-page behaviour the retained client has always had, and whether the
native client should match it is a product question this witness does not
settle.
The answer is asked to begin with FIRSTLINE so the top of the answer
carries a marker worth waiting for. `1` would match a hundred other rows.
BE EXACT ABOUT WHAT THAT MATCH PROVES. The submitted prompt also contains
the word, and its echo sits immediately ABOVE the answer, so the assertion
is satisfied by the answer's first row or by the prompt echo one row
further back — not by one specific occurrence. Both are on the far side of
the 300 lines the view had to cross, so what is established is that the
view reached the TOP OF THE ANSWER, which is the reachability claim.
The return is thirty PageDowns, at least as many as either client spent
going up. PageDown clamps at the TAIL, which is where the `300` assertion
needs the view to be, so a surplus is safe and a deficit would land short
and report a defect that is not there. That assertion is shared because by
then both clients are pinned to the same end of the transcript.
The navigation prefix is copied from j04-comparative, so both scenarios
select the SAME model and this run is inside the matched-model claim.

steps.capture: the model choice, where the two clients differ most

steps.paste: Reply with the word FIRSTLINE and then count from one to three hundred, one number per line, with no other commentary.

native: the top of the answer, after twelve pages
retained: the top of the answer, after thirty half-pages
